    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.

edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;

  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

A set S is a clique in G iff its complement V\S is a vertex cover of the complement graph, so a clique of size ≥ k exists iff a vertex cover of size ≤ n−k exists. I'll write `reduce.py` accordingly, handling all edge cases automatically via the n−k budget.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-mpncuh4s && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover.

Given a Clique instance
    {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
we build the complement graph H on the same vertex set 0..n-1 and output the
Vertex Cover instance
    {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": n - k}.

Correctness:
    A set C is a vertex cover of H
        iff V \\ C is an independent set in H
        iff V \\ C is a clique in G.
    Hence G has a clique of size at least k
        iff H has a vertex cover of size at most n - k.

The construction is polynomial: it examines O(n^2) vertex pairs.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Reduce a Clique instance to a Vertex Cover instance."""
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Normalize the given edges (undirected, no self-loops) into a set.
    given = set()
    for u, v in instance["edges"]:
        if u > v:
            u, v = v, u
        given.add((u, v))

    # Edges of the complement graph: all pairs not present in G.
    complement_edges = []
    for u in range(n):
        for v in range(u + 1, n):
            if (u, v) not in given:
                complement_edges.append([u, v])

    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": n - k}
EOF
cat reduce.py"}

    k = instance["k"]

    given = set()

            u, v = v, u
        given.add((u, v))
